- If sentiment is negative (e.g., -0.25) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- If model shows early sharp downward spike (e.g., 65.51, 64.00), it often underestimates subsequent rally; add a small upward bias in next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or positive (0.00), model frequently overestimates short-term volatility; smooth out forecast peaks and valleys.
- Model tends to underestimate late-period price action (last 7–10 days of 30d forecast) — especially after initial spike — so apply a slight upward bias to final 5–7 days.
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 68.27 → 67.63 → 68.40 → 68.83 → 68.49 → 67.86 → 67.34), model often fails to recognize the pattern; adjust forecast to reflect gradual reversion toward prior mean.
- When sentiment is positive (e.g., 0.50) followed by negative (e.g., -0.25), model often overreacts to the negative sentiment; dampen the forecast dip and allow for a slower correction.
